|strategy=By Tom Lischke<ref name="decipher-strategy">https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/anewhope/dark/small/ghhhk.html</ref>

Dark Side C2 [[A New Hope]]

[[Ghhhk]] and its lightside counterpart, [[Houjix]], open up a whole new type of deck construction with the release of [[A New Hope]]. In the Premiere set, 'getting wide' to augment force drains was a dangerous proposition. Having only one or two characters or starships at each location invited an overwhelming counterattack, with a huge amount of battle damage typically resulting. Even if the player being attacked had an interrupt to cancel the battle, there was always the danger that the attacker had a [[Sense (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Sense]] to cancel the [[Hyper Escape]] or [[Narrow Escape]]. [[Ghhhk]] now allows the loser of the battle to eliminate all battle damage. It is immune to [[Sense (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Sense]], so the worst thing the LS player can do is hit it with What Are You Tryin To Push On Us or [[Grappling Hook]]. With eight to ten Ghhhks in a deck, the DS player can include many locations and cheap characters/starships to get a good force drain established before the LS can respond. When Obi, [[Luke Skywalker{{!}}Luke]], and [[Han Solo{{!}}Han]] (along with the [[Jedi Presence]] and Destiny Adders) show up to attack that [[Stormtrooper]] draining in the [[Tatooine: Cantina (Dark){{!}}Cantina]] with a Presence of the Force for 3 a turn, the DS can forfeit the [[Stormtrooper]] and play [[Ghhhk]] to eliminate the battle damage. For spice, she can play a [[Lone Warrior]] to force the LS to lose [[Han Solo{{!}}Han]]. The next turn, the DS can continue draining at the other 4 [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]] sites in play. If the LS player spreads thin to try to stop the drain, DS may respond by playing that [[Darth Vader{{!}}Vader]] or [[Kitik Keed'kak]] they have been holding. This strategy works extremely well in space also. The key is having enough locations and cheap deploys in the deck to maintain the force drain throughout the game. And most importantly, always have a [[Ghhhk]] in hand.

Cards to watch out for: [[Grimtaash]]. The DS should stop drawing when there are two or three Ghhhks in hand, or run the risk of having the deck crippled by this card. [[Grappling Hook]]. If one of the Ghhhks gets grappled, the DS should make sure adequate forfeit is maintained at all sites to avoid a debilitating battle loss.

Combos:

[[Ghhhk]] + Stormtroopers (TIEs) (Jawas) + [[Lone Warrior]] ([[Lone Pilot]]) ([[Moment Of Triumph]]). One of the keys to the force drain deck is maintaining more characters or ships on the table. It helps to add some attrition to knock off a few of the LS characters or ships.

[[Ghhhk]] + WED 15-17 'Septoid droid'. Adding a few of these attrition soaks can help protect some of the stronger characters in the deck. If the attack continues next turn, maybe [[Ghhhk]] will become necessary. These work well at sites where the DS has established 4 ability, and thus, a destiny draw.

[[Ghhhk]] + [[Presence Of The Force]] + [[Organa's Ceremonial Necklace]]. These cards help the force drain. They fit better in a [[Ghhhk]] deck than a lightsaber because the 'saber has to be protected. The point of playing with [[Ghhhk]] is that the DS player does not mind losing any given character or ship.

[[Ghhhk]] + [[Imperial Holotable]] + [[Monnok]] + [[Ng'ok]]. Just another site to force drain at. Just one [[Ghhhk]] can keep the LS player from draining there every turn as the DS can deploy on her turn, and withdraw during the LS deploy phase.

[[Ghhhk]] + [[Mosep]]. [[Mosep]] should be one of the prime force drain members, as the loss will come straight from the LS reserve deck.

[[Ghhhk]] + [[Sunsdown]] + [[Defel]]. [[Defel]] under night time conditions fits the theme of this deck perfectly, as he can avoid combat, thus saving the use of the [[Ghhhk]], and still be there for the counter attack.

8/21/96

These cards are extremely versatile and can almost always help add to your force drain or lessen your opponents.

Here's how.

If you're getting Force drained for 3 or more (the more the better) at any site, deploy a talz/stormtrooper/x-wing/tie or other similar low deploy card. You will then block the force drain on your opponents turn. He/she will then have to spend a Force to initiate (mabye more if he targets weapons, etc.). You merely lose the one card and the [[Houjix]]/[[Ghhhk]]. Thus, if he/she was going to Force drain for five you would instead lose only the [[Houjix]] and character.

Another great use for these cards is the following. Pick a remote spot (a site with no adjacent areas) where you can Force drain for one or, if possible, two. If you have a spy, look for a 2/0 Force site (war room). Deploy a character there. Your opponent will be forced to deploy characters to block the Force drain and then battle you. When he/she does, lose your two cards. He/she has used up a good deal of Force killing your character and has now stranded (barring a Nabrun/Elis) one or more characters on this remote site. If it is a 2/0 site then he/she can't force drain either.

These cards are also a must if you use undercover spies. If your opponent Alters your [[Undercover (Dark){{!}}Undercover]] effect, you will most likely be caught with just one card defending against a rather large group. Without the [[Houjix]]/Ghhk cards you could lose a good deal of Force.
